input: Read /data/users_v1.json containing user records in API v1 format. Transform each record to v2 format: combine 'firstName' and 'lastName' into a single 'fullName' field (space-separated), rename 'emailAddress' to 'email', extract the 'city' from the nested 'address' object into a top-level 'location' field, and add a 'migrated' boolean field set to true. Keep the 'id' field. Save the v2 array to /data/users_v2.json and print it.

transcript.final_response:
I converted all three user records to v2 format and saved the array to `/data/users_v2.json`. This is the saved file:

```json
[
  {"id": 1, "fullName": "Alice Smith", "email": "alice@example.com", "location": "Seattle", "migrated": true},
  {"id": 2, "fullName": "Bob Jones", "email": "bob@example.com", "location": "Portland", "migrated": true},
  {"id": 3, "fullName": "Carol Davis", "email": "carol@example.com", "location": "Denver", "migrated": true}
]
```

The file itself is pretty-printed by `jq`, so each record spans several lines. I condensed it here to save space.

Each record now has `fullName` (first and last name joined by a space), `email` (renamed from `emailAddress`), `location` (the city from `address`) and `migrated: true`, and it keeps its `id`. The rest of the `address` object (street and state) is dropped, since you only asked for the city.
tool_calls: jq '[.[] | {id, fullName: (.firstName + " " + .lastName), email: .emailAddress, location: .address.city, migrated: true}]' /data/users_v1.json > /data/users_v2.json; cat /data/users_v2.json
